notes.1: The source heading is X. The complete printed pages62–63 show alternating verse insets, retained after actual line-start inspection.
notes.3: The source prints commas after Flava and Ceres and at the end of the verse.
notes.9: Oracula prima is set off with commas, and the verse ends with a colon.
notes.12: The printed reading is subsecuitque; at14 it is revellit. These source forms are retained.
notes.15: The source prints amantum; the next verse has secubituque.
notes.19: The parenthesis opens after the semicolon and continues across the page break through alumno at23. It is preserved as printed punctuation rather than a physical alteration.
notes.20: The source names Crete and Iove, with a terminal colon; no letter is supplied to modernize the names.
notes.25: The printed name is Iasium, followed by Cretaea diva sub Ida.
notes.28: The source has Hinc pudor, ex illa parte trahebat amor: with a terminal colon.
notes.29: There is a period after pudor followed by lowercase sulcos, retained as printed.
notes.31: The contracted printed form is pulsarant, not an expanded spelling.
notes.34: The source spelling is Inrita, retained without normalization.
notes.36: The source reads Deciderant longae spicea serta comae.
notes.39: The printed form is canebat, retained as written, with Idae at the end.
notes.42: The comma follows Optavit. Cereris longus ut esset amor is retained in source order.
notes.45: The printed edition encloses45–46 in square brackets, including the question mark at46. This is printed editorial enclosure, not manuscript cancellation or erasure.
notes.48: A period follows deos; the small nearby uneven dark spot is not treated as a separate printed punctuation sign. Heading XI. and the next poem begin below48 on printed page63.
